meaning.zh:
“非常高兴” 或 “乐得合不拢嘴”。

这个短语的来历并无确切的出处，但可以追溯到20世纪早期。词源学家推测该表达法源于当人们非常开心或受宠若惊时，脸上会泛起一种红晕，这种颜色与粉色相似，因此得名 “tickled pink”。这个表达法常用于描述极其愉快、非常开心的情感状态。
meaning.en: This idiom doesn't have a precise origin but can be traced back to the early 20th century. Etymologists suggest that the expression comes from the idea that when people are very happy or delighted, their faces might develop a pinkish blush, hence "tickled pink." It is used to describe an extreme state of happiness or delight.

lines.en: She was *tickled pink* when she found out she had won the contest.
lines.zh: 她得知自己赢得比赛时，开心得不得了。

lines.en: I'm *tickled pink* to see you here tonight!
lines.zh: 今晚见到你，我高兴极了！

lines.en: They were *tickled pink* with their new puppy.
lines.zh: 他们对新小狗高兴得合不拢嘴。
